conflict_topics: unclean shared dishes / responsibility for washing
kitchen cooking odors spreading to bedrooms
stove scheduling / competing cooking times on weeknights
dialogue_quality_notes: Natural, concise roommate-style exchanges; participants move from complaint to practical proposals rather quickly.
There are multiple short confirmation checks (Rounds 6–8) restating the same commitments, producing minor repetition.
Speakers stay consistent with roles and facts (who cooked, who complained, who proposed rules).
Resolutions are pragmatic (ventilation, wash-up, heads-up) rather than formal rule-making.
evaluation.final_reason: Participants proposed and accepted simple behavioral rules but did not produce explicit, unanimous spoken agreement from every household member on every point. Key lines: B proposed ventilation: "Can we at least use the fan and open the window when cooking?" (Turn 7). C agreed and added cleaning: "That's fair. Can we also agree to wash up right after we cook?" (Turn 8). D endorsed the points and proposed scheduling: "For the stove, could we just give a heads-up in the group chat when we plan to cook?" (Turn 9). A accepted the group-chat idea: "Yeah, that's fine." (Turn 10) and later reconfirmed "Yes." (Turn 15). Because some participants (notably A for fan/window and the others for the group chat) never explicitly voiced full acceptance on every measure in the transcript, the outcome is partial: several measures are agreed in principle (fan/window, wash-up, group-chat heads-up) but not fully and unanimously confirmed in the conversation.
position_change_notes: Agent A: Initially defensive about the pan (Turn 1: "...It's not mine."), later accepts the group-chat heads-up (Turn 10: "Yeah, that's fine." and Turn 15: "Yes.").
Agent D: Moves from complaint about scheduling (Turn 3/5) to proposing a concrete solution (Turn 9: group-chat heads-up) and endorses ventilation/wash-up (Turn 9: "Yeah, those are good points.").
Agent C: Begins by noting the unwashed pan (Turn 2) and then endorses ventilation and proposes washing up after cooking (Turn 8).
Agent B: Raises the odor problem and repeatedly seeks clear agreement on ventilation (Turns 7, 12, 17) but does not have to change position; instead prompts others to accept concrete measures.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: "That pan's from last night. It's not mine." vs Turn 2 — Agent C: "I don't know whose it is either. Things just get left here." Substantive disagreement about responsibility for the unwashed pan and a general complaint about things being left.

Turn 3 — Agent D: "It's not just the cleaning. By the time I get home, the stove is busy until late." vs Turn 4 — Agent A: "I have to eat, too. This is when I finish work." Clear incompatible practical interests over when the stove should be used.

Turn 5 — Agent D: "Right, but that's the problem. If we all just cook when we get home, the last person has to wait hours." followed by Turn 6 — Agent A: "So what do you suggest?" The disagreement remains but participants are asking for a solution rather than escalating demands.

Turn 7 — Agent B: "Can we at least use the fan and open the window when cooking? The smell is going all the way to my room." and Turn 8 — Agent C: "That's fair. Can we also agree to wash up right after we cook?" Proposal and partial acceptance reduce the conflict but not everyone has explicitly agreed yet.

Turn 9 — Agent D: "Yeah, those are good points. For the stove, could we just give a heads-up in the group chat when we plan to cook?" and Turn 10 — Agent A: "Yeah, that's fine." The group-chat heads-up is proposed and A accepts; other participants have not all explicitly confirmed every element yet.

Turn 12 — Agent B: "Okay, but what about the fan and the window? Are we all doing that?" and Turn 13 — Agent C: "Yes. Fan and window when you cook, wash up when you're done." Further explicit endorsement by C reduces friction but not everyone has said so aloud.

Turn 14 — Agent D: "Okay, so the group chat heads-up is okay with everyone too?" and Turn 15 — Agent A: "Yes." The group-chat idea has A and D on record accepting it; a couple of participants haven't explicitly confirmed in the transcript.

Turn 17 — Agent B: "Okay, but are we all agreeing to the fan and window too?" and Turn 19 — Agent D: "Yes, I'm fine with the fan and window. Are you fine with the group chat?" More confirmation, but not every participant has explicitly voiced full agreement on every point, so a small unresolved element remains.

substantive_insights: Two distinct practical tensions underlie the conflict: odors/cleaning versus timing/access to the stove.
Simple behavioral rules (use fan/window, wash up immediately, give a chat heads-up) are sufficient to address the main issues in principle.
Participants quickly moved from stating grievances to proposing and accepting low-cost behavioral fixes, which reduced friction even without formal enforcement.
Lack of explicit, unanimous verbal agreement left a small outstanding uncertainty about whether everyone will follow the new practices.
